ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 1.2 meters. It is olive-green or yellowish above with a pale, unmarked belly and a distinct, dark post-ocular stripe. Its large eyes feature vertical, cat-like pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Boiga flaviviridis* is its uniform yellowish-green dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct dark crossbands or blotches found on other Indian *Boiga* species.
ai.habitat: *Boiga flaviviridis* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations up to 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellow-green Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for geckos and small lizards among tree branches and rocky crevices under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga flaviviridis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 5–10 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, roughly from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga flaviviridis* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the states of Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh across dry deciduous forests and scrublands.
